host_pilot.interpretation: Mixed observed task outcomes with higher token/request usage for extra instructions in all three pairs. No demonstrated consistent benefit; the optional instructions are not promoted to the default or injected into frozen feedback conditions.
limitations: Three related native train tasks, one realization per condition; tasks5/8 share user/policy context, so not three independent source confirmations.
Later simulator replies diverged and sometimes violated frozen task rules; this is closed-loop behavior, not a fixed-readout estimate.
Native final-state score is distinct from dialogue/task/UX correctness; official task/UX judge was not run, and no substitute scalar author reward or training labels were created.
All runs had no memory tool; this is not evidence for or against Jev/MiLAi quality.
Model GPU time and monetary cost are not priced; earlier/unmeasured interpreter startup, authoring, inspection, reporting and settlement overhead remain unknown, not zero.
Equal descriptive native pass counts do not establish equivalence; task outcomes and failure mechanisms differ.
